annotations.title: General Assembly Adopts Resolution Calling upon States Not to Recognize Changes in Status of Crimea Region | Meetings Coverage and Press Releases

content.text:
**Under international law and by the position of most countries, Crimea does *not* belong to Russia; it is recognized as part of Ukraine.** Russia has controlled and administered Crimea since its 2014 annexation, but that annexation is widely considered illegal and is not recognized by the UN General Assembly, the United States, the EU, Ukraine, and many other states.

The key distinction is:

- **De jure / legal status:** Crimea is part of **Ukraine**.
- **De facto / actual control:** Crimea is currently controlled by **Russia**.

In 2014, the UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity and called on states not to recognize any change in Crimea’s status after the Russian-backed referendum. ([press.un.org](https://press.un.org/en/2014/ga11493.doc.htm?utm_source=openai))
